workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
rationale: The watchdog's asynchronous set has priority over rst_ni, so reset does not initialise fault_q while the fault input is asserted.

author_reading.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
author_reading.rationale: The watchdog asynchronous set has priority over reset, so asserting wdog_fault_i while rst_ni is low sets fault_q and the reset is not honoured.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: The asynchronous set from wdog_fault_i has priority over rst_ni, since the set branch is tested first. While the watchdog is asserted, reset cannot clear fault_q, so the stored fault survives reset and the state is not initialised.
labels.suspected_flaw: Whether reset should dominate a live watchdog fault is a design decision the case does not state. The RTL gives set priority, which is a likely error.

labels.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
labels.rationale: Watchdog set dominates while both controls are asserted. When the watchdog drops while reset remains asserted, no asynchronous event clears fault_q and the fault can remain visible until a clock edge.

settlement.workflow_class: Asynchronous control conflicts and reset as data
settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical, class and RDC-026. Their extra RDC-002/RDC-003/RDC-011 rules are incidental. Sites merge A's line 11 and B's line 12.
